bio: NorthSideBenji is a Brampton rapper whose music balances street detail with melody and a low-key delivery that rarely needs to force the point. His catalogue has made him one of the steadier voices in the GTA's melodic rap lane, with songs built around reflective writing, clipped hooks and production that leaves room for his voice. In 2026 he joined Boi-1da and Canada Soccer for TRYNA WIN, part of the WHAT IF IT ALL GOES RIGHT? project, and followed it with more new material including Crowd Control.

Norwill Simmonds is a Jamaican-born, Canada-based gospel singer, songwriter and broadcaster who has spent decades making music in Ontario. After beginning to record as a child in Jamaica, he settled in Canada, recorded three gospel albums here and became host of Morning Dew Gospel Music on iLive Toronto. He is also the father of Daniel Caesar; his vocal and songwriting feature on Caesar's Baby Blue is the Northern Dial library credit.
Iranian-born, Canadian-raised DJ, producer and rapper Nostalgix emerged from Vancouver's electronic scene with high-energy bass house shaped by 1990s pop and hip-hop influences.
Montréal-born, Toronto-raised rapper, singer and producer Notifi is a Canadian artist whose dark pop, R&B and hip-hop reflect the Scarborough and Jane-Finch communities where he grew up.

Nowfolk is the Vancouver underground hip-hop duo of Moka Only and Ishkan. Emerging from the City Planners/Torchlight Commission orbit, the pair began recording together in the late 1990s and released projects including Style Gangstas, The Moon, The Winter. From 2001 and Magnesium Opium.

Rwandan-Canadian rapper, poet and activist Ntwali Kayijaho came up in Edmonton's hip-hop community before expanding his creative circle in Montréal. His socially conscious music draws on family history, Black identity, resilience and community advocacy, with projects including New Beginnings and performances that bridge music and motivational speaking.
Vancouver-born producer NXSTY, born Bowen Sanderson, is a Canadian electronic artist known for heavy trap, bass house and high-impact festival production.
Toronto-born artist, musician, songwriter and producer O'Sound, born Owen Lee, is a Canadian R&B, soul and gospel vocalist whose career also includes extensive work in Nova Scotia's music community.
Hamilton-born rapper, producer and comedian OB OBrien, born Matthew O'Brien, is a Canadian hip-hop artist best known for his longtime association with Drake and OVO.

Oche is a Lagos-born, Toronto-based singer, rapper, songwriter and producer whose music blends alternative R&B, soul and hip-hop. His work moves between melodic songwriting and rap while drawing on his Nigerian roots and Toronto surroundings. Northern Dial carries Oche as part of its contemporary Canadian R&B and hip-hop catalogue.
Guyanese-born, Toronto-based rapper, broadcaster and curator Odario leads the hip-hop project Grand Analog while exploring alternative dance, experimental rap and wide-ranging musical storytelling.

Odds formed in Vancouver in 1987 around Craig Northey, Steven Drake, Doug Elliott and Paul Brennan, sharpening their songwriting while also working the local circuit as the cover band Dawn Patrol. A move through Los Angeles showcases led to a deal with Zoo Entertainment and the 1991 debut Neopolitan. The 1993 follow-up Bedbugs pushed the band further into Canadian rock radio with songs including "Heterosexual Man" and "It Falls Apart," while a touring relationship with Warren Zevon, for whom Odds served as both opening act and backing band, reflected the group's unusually strong songwriting credentials.

Good Weird Feeling became the band's commercial peak in Canada, reaching platinum status and producing a run of sharp, melodic singles, while 1996's Nest added "Someone Who's Cool" and "Make You Mad." At a time when alternative rock was often defined by heaviness, Odds leaned into power-pop economy, vocal interplay and dry humour. That made them one of Vancouver's most distinctive 1990s guitar bands and gave their songs a character that remained recognizable after the original lineup's late-decade hiatus.

Odds returned in 2008 with Cheerleader and continued releasing music, including Universal Remote and the 2023 album Crash the Time Machine. They also built a substantial parallel life in film and television music, including work connected to The Kids in the Hall and Corner Gas. The band's significance lies in that combination of craft and longevity: a deep catalogue of concise, witty rock songs that moved comfortably between radio, live performance and Canadian screen culture instead of being trapped in one 1990s moment.

OLIVER is the electronic production duo of Vaughn Oliver and Oliver Goldstein. Northern Dial carries the duo's 2017 track 'Go With It' from the album Full Circle. Vaughn Oliver is a Canadian producer originally associated with Vancouver, and the duo's catalogue blends electro, nu-disco and pop production. Northern Dial retains OLIVER in its Canadian catalogue based on Vaughn Oliver's Canadian identity and the exact Full Circle recording credit.
Winnipeg-born Canadian singer-songwriter Olivia Lunny makes melodic alt-pop built around bright synth production, indie-pop textures and dance-ready hooks.

Olivia Ridgely is a Montreal-based Canadian indie-pop singer and songwriter whose catalogue includes releases such as Busy Body, Flowers for a Friend, Blu/Lucky, Hot Cakes and twenty18. Her work also extends into collaborations across Canadian pop, folk and electronic music, including songs with Theo Day and Montreal artists. Northern Dial carries Olivia Ridgely as part of its contemporary Canadian indie-pop catalogue.
Toronto-born, Brampton-based artist Omega Mighty blends Caribbean influence, pop, R&B and dance music with a performance background spanning vocals, piano and dance.

Only1KNG is a Canadian producer and musician whose work is closely connected to Toronto's independent hip-hop and R&B community. He has produced and performed with artists including Junia-T, Tea Fannie, STORRY, Samalong and Borelson, contributing keyboards, production and collaborative releases across Canadian projects. Northern Dial carries Only1KNG as part of its contemporary Canadian producer catalogue.

ORA is a Montreal experimental electronic duo formed by sound artists Stéphanie Castonguay and Maxime Corbeil-Perron. Their work combines prepared instruments, electronics, electromagnetic field sensors and improvised sound, with releases through Montreal label Mikroclimat. Northern Dial carries ORA as part of its experimental Quebec electronic catalogue.
Vancouver Island singer-songwriter Ora Cogan is a Canadian folk and experimental artist whose music blends haunted acoustic songwriting with psychedelia, country and darkwave textures.

Orange Gecko is a Montreal francophone pop-rock group whose music mixes soul, jazz, indie pop and groove-driven rock. Formed in 2016, the Quebec group has released projects including Amour et stupéfiants and Jab!, evolving through several lineups while remaining part of Montreal's independent music scene.

Orlanda is Montréal artist Orlanda Gagnon, a francophone singer-songwriter and vocalist whose solo catalogue includes the EP Fantaisie. Northern Dial's Orlanda entry is tied to Marco Ema's 'Comme un refrain' from Soleil mâché, whose official credits list Orlanda Gagnon on vocals. Her solo work is also catalogued by Québec music-industry source PalmarèsADISQ.
Toronto-based Nigerian-Canadian singer Osé blends Afrobeat, alternative R&B, soul and gospel and broke through with the viral 2024 single Makaveli.
French Guianan-born, Montréal-based musician Ouri is a classically trained producer, DJ and multi-instrumentalist who brings orchestral composition into experimental electronic pop and R&B.
Canadian singer and rapper OVI WOOD makes contemporary R&B and melodic hip-hop built around raw emotion, intimate writing and atmospheric production.
Mildmay, Ontario singer-songwriter Owen Riegling makes contemporary Canadian country rooted in small-town storytelling, traditional country textures and modern country-pop hooks.
Toronto rapper P Reign, later known as Preme, built a Canadian hip-hop career around street-oriented rap, major-label releases and collaborations with artists including Drake and Future.

Papi AQ is a Mexican-born, Toronto-based Latin-Canadian singer and rapper who moved to Canada in the early 2000s. Performing in English and Spanish, he developed a self-described Spanglish sound shaped by his Toronto upbringing and has built a catalogue spanning hip-hop, trap, R&B and Latin music through releases including BODMON, Rumba and Keys to My City.

Toronto-born rapper Paris Richards is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose music draws on her experiences as a young mother, model and former exotic dancer. After beginning to record seriously in the mid-2010s, she built a catalogue around bold, self-directed writing and released projects including Queen of the 6ix, positioning her work around women's independence, sexuality and survival.

Scarborough MC Parker is a member of Monolith, the Canadian hip-hop collective formed in Toronto in the mid-1990s. He appears with the crew on recordings including Wio-K’s Ten and Grimace Love’s Perception-era material, part of the interconnected catalogue that made Monolith a fixture of Toronto underground rap.

Mississauga singer, songwriter and producer PARTYNEXTDOOR became the first artist signed to Drake’s OVO Sound label in 2013 and quickly helped define the label’s atmospheric approach to contemporary R&B. His self-titled debut project and PARTYNEXTDOOR TWO paired sparse production, blurred vocals and Caribbean rhythmic influence with emotionally detached relationship writing. Songs such as “Break from Toronto” and “Recognize” established a solo audience while connecting his sound directly to the broader Toronto R&B ecosystem.

His influence grew even further through songwriting and production for other artists. PARTYNEXTDOOR co-wrote Rihanna’s “Work,” a nine-week Billboard Hot 100 No. 1, and contributed to major records for artists including DJ Khaled, Beyoncé, Post Malone and Usher. His Drake collaboration “Come and See Me” earned a GRAMMY nomination for Best R&B Song, while later projects including PARTYNEXTDOOR 3, PARTYMOBILE and PARTYNEXTDOOR 4 continued his own catalogue alongside behind-the-scenes writing.

That dual career is central to his significance. PARTYNEXTDOOR is both a key architect of the moody, minimal Toronto R&B sound associated with OVO and a pop songwriter whose ideas travelled far outside that scene. In 2024, the National Music Publishers Association named him its top artist-songwriter for the second quarter after a run of major U.S. certifications, underscoring how much of his impact exists both on his own records and inside other artists’ hits.

Passion Mango is a Vancouver indie and bedroom-pop project led by songwriter and musician Connor Wilkinson. The project's dreamy sound combines indie pop, lo-fi textures and melodic songwriting. Northern Dial carries Passion Mango as part of its contemporary British Columbia independent music catalogue.
Montréal-raised singer-songwriter, pianist and composer Patrick Watson makes lush chamber-pop and experimental indie music and won the Polaris Music Prize for Close to Paradise.

Montreal-born, Toronto-raised rapper and multidisciplinary artist Patrik Kabongo brings together hip-hop, pop and independent entrepreneurship through his X10 creative platform. His work reflects both his Congolese family roots and the Canadian cities that shaped him.
Campbellton, New Brunswick-born singer and actor Patsy Gallant is a bilingual Acadian-Canadian performer whose decades-long career includes pop, disco and musical theatre.

Pay$o is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose catalogue includes tracks such as Digital Minds, St-Antoine, Dollarama, Rudimentary and Game Changer. His music draws on contemporary urban rap while reflecting everyday life and personal experience, and he has appeared alongside other Montreal-linked independent artists. Northern Dial carries Pay$o as part of its contemporary Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Toronto rapper Pengz emerged from the city's street-rap scene through collaborations with TwoTwo, including Griselda Blanco, before building a solo run around his distinct clipped flow on tracks such as Alejandro Sosa and Igloo.
Canadian rapper Peter Jackson built a long-running independent hip-hop career through extensive touring, collaborations and releases connecting Canada's rap scene with major U.S. artists.

Québec singer-songwriter Peter Peter makes French-language alternative pop and indie rock built around synths, guitars, melancholy melodies and an increasing pull toward club-oriented electronic music.

PHB Hollis is a Canadian hip-hop artist connected to Brampton-rooted Capital Vision and the wider Toronto-area rap scene. His catalogue includes singles such as 'Switched Up' and 'Same Thing,' along with Capital Vision collaborations including 'Lost Time,' 'Pray For Me,' 'Wild Life' and 'Soul Complete.' Northern Dial carries PHB Hollis as part of its emerging GTA hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto artist pHoenix Pagliacci is a Canadian rapper, R&B singer, producer and advocate known for solo work and membership in The Sorority and TRP.P.

Alma-born singer-songwriter Pierre Lapointe is a leading Québec chanson artist whose work combines francophone pop tradition with modern arrangements, theatrical presentation and contemporary songwriting.
Regina rapper Pimpton, born Kyriel Roberts, is a Trinidad-born Canadian hip-hop artist whose independent career has helped build Saskatchewan's contemporary rap scene.

Ajax-born, Toronto-based singer-songwriter and producer Pino is part of a new generation of Canadian R&B artists reviving the warmth of early-2000s soul and R&B through modern production. His 2025 EP '02 features Toronto collaborators including Dylan Sinclair, Avenoir, Maz B and Norah's World and reflects the community-oriented approach of the city's emerging R&B scene.
Montréal trio Planet Giza blends hip-hop with funk and jazz through rapper Tony Stone and producers Rami B and DoomX, earning Polaris Music Prize recognition for its genre-fluid work.

Hamilton, Ontario alternative-rock band playingwithfire formed in 2020 around vocalist-guitarist Campbell Coleman and drummer Brandon Roussell, later expanding with keyboardist Robert Bisset. With the pandemic limiting conventional rehearsals and live development during the group’s earliest period, much of its initial songwriting took shape remotely before the band moved into regular performance and recording.

The group’s sound draws from several strands of modern rock rather than a single revival lane, combining gritty guitar work with post-punk melody, electronic-rock textures and introspective songwriting. Early songs such as "Shivering" established that approach, while later releases pushed toward a darker and more atmospheric presentation. In 2026 the band issued the five-track project Monologues at Midnight, including "Erased," "Silhouette" and "Fallback."

playingwithfire is still an emerging act, so its significance is less about established awards than about documenting a developing Ontario rock voice while the story is still unfolding. Northern Dial’s profile captures the band at that stage: locally grounded, independently built and still defining how far its hybrid alternative-rock sound can travel.
Toronto singer-songwriter PLAZA makes atmospheric alternative R&B built around hushed vocals, nocturnal production and emotionally distant, late-night songwriting.

Pluto was a Vancouver alternative-rock band formed in 1993 by Ian Jones, Rolf Hetherington, John Ounpuu and Justin Leigh. After early independent and Mint Records releases, the group signed with Virgin Records and earned a 1997 Juno nomination for Best New Group. Paste, from the band's 1996 self-titled album, is the Pluto recording in the Northern Dial library.

Point Blank grew out of Toronto's Regent Park in the early 1990s, with a large crew of emcees and producer Pikihed using rap to document the neighbourhood around them. The group developed outside the major-label system and built its own Tilt Rock Records infrastructure, giving songs about policing, poverty, family pressure and street life a platform that did not depend on the Canadian industry's limited support for rap. Early releases such as "Retaliation" and the Point Blank Underground collection established a catalogue rooted as much in place and community as in individual personalities.

During the 2000s, Point Blank became increasingly visible beyond Regent Park without abandoning that perspective. "Thin Line" and "Want It Wit Us" earned radio and MuchMusic attention, while "Born and Raised in the Ghetto" became the group's signature statement and received a MuchMusic Video Award nomination. Their long-awaited self-titled 2008 album arrived through Tilt Rock and Koch Entertainment Canada, bringing years of independent material and local momentum into a national release. The record was nominated for Rap Recording of the Year at the 2009 JUNO Awards.

Point Blank's significance is inseparable from Regent Park itself. Long before redevelopment transformed the neighbourhood and before Toronto street rap became an internationally watched scene, the group was using self-owned infrastructure to put Regent Park stories into circulation on Canadian radio, television and record shelves. Their career offers a direct line from 1990s neighbourhood-based independent rap to a later Toronto culture in which local identity, entrepreneurship and highly specific geography became central parts of how artists presented themselves.
Toronto artist Poizunus is a Canadian beatboxer, DJ and producer who has competed internationally, appeared on MuchMusic and become a veteran figure in Canada's beatboxing community.
